chains.name: Canton
chains.model: Need-to-know by design. Each institution runs its own node; only the nodes in a trade see it, with messages encrypted end to end.
chains.hides: Trade content from every node not in the trade.
chains.visible: The synchronizer orders encrypted messages and sees metadata, not trade content.
chains.fee_note: median transaction, gross, before rewards returned to operators (draft CIP)

chains.name: Ethereum
chains.model: Application-level privacy: Privacy Pools (0xbow), a screened shielded pool that added private in-pool payments in its October 2026 v2, plus other shielded pools; the Ethereum Foundation has committed to privacy as a protocol priority.
chains.hides: Sender, recipient and amount of transfers inside the pool, and the link between deposit and withdrawal.
chains.visible: Deposits into and withdrawals out of the pool; everything outside it is public. A screening provider approves deposits.

chains.name: Polygon PoS
chains.model: Private payments for stablecoins (USDC and USDT) on the public chain, through Hinkal's shielded pool with screening on every transfer.
chains.hides: Sender, receiver and amount; senders and receivers cannot be linked on-chain.

chains.name: Solana
chains.model: Confidential transfers in the Token-2022 program, using zero-knowledge proofs. Switched off in June 2025 after a bug in the proofs; back on with Agave 4.0 in June 2026.

chains.name: Aztec
chains.model: Private execution: smart contracts with private state, settled to Ethereum.
chains.hides: Contract state and execution details, by default.
chains.visible: What a contract chooses to make public.

chains.name: ZKsync Prividium
chains.model: A private, permissioned chain per operator; transaction data stays off the public chain, with validity proofs posted to Ethereum.
chains.hides: All transaction data from the public.
chains.visible: Proofs and state commitments on Ethereum; the operator controls access to the data.

chains.name: Hedera
chains.model: HashSphere private networks for institutions, alongside Hedera's published transaction privacy design.
chains.hides: Everything on a private network from outsiders.
chains.visible: What the network operator chooses to anchor or share.
chains.fee_note: public network, token transfer (published fee schedule)

chains.name: Avalanche
chains.model: Encrypted ERC-20 (eERC): zero-knowledge proofs plus homomorphic encryption in an ordinary contract, with no protocol change. Can issue a private token or wrap an existing ERC-20. Private permissioned Avalanche L1s are also available.
chains.visible: The transaction and the accounts that send it, as with any contract call.

chains.name: Aptos
chains.model: Confidential APT: balances held encrypted in a protocol pool, with proofs checked by validators. Only APT so far.
chains.visible: Addresses, asset type, timing, and amounts moving in or out of the pool. An optional governance-set auditor can read amounts.

chains.name: Aleo
chains.model: Private by default: a zero-knowledge chain where transfers spend encrypted records. Circle's USDCx stablecoin is live, backed 1:1 through Circle's xReserve.
chains.visible: That a transaction happened, and transfers between public and private balances. USDCx includes compliance monitoring and a freeze-list check.

chains.name: Stellar
chains.model: X-Ray zero-knowledge building blocks went live on mainnet in January 2026 (Protocol 25); confidential tokens reached testnet in August 2026, and OpenZeppelin shipped the audited contracts in October. Not yet approved for mainnet.
chains.visible: Today, transfers are public. When live: addresses, and amounts moving in or out of confidential balances.

chains.name: XRP Ledger
chains.since: in validator vote (21 of 35 for, 28 needed, Nov 2026)
chains.model: Confidential multi-purpose tokens (XLS-96), proposed as a protocol amendment.

chains.name: Arc (Circle)
chains.model: Opt-in privacy with built-in auditability, on the roadmap; mainnet launched without it.

chains.name: Hyperledger Besu
chains.model: Private networks are private by nature: only members can read them. Built-in private transactions (Tessera) were removed in release 25.6.0.
chains.visible: Every member of the network sees every transaction unless access is restricted further.
